editorial:
Imagine you are a huge fan of a famous author who refuses to write anymore. That is where you start with this story. You follow a young guy who flies all the way from New York to Switzerland just to beg Patricia Highsmith to write one more Tom Ripley book. At first, it feels like a quiet drama about art and fame, but the vibe quickly shifts. As the two characters spend more time together, the young man stops being a fan and starts becoming a threat. It is a creepy game of cat and mouse where you never quite know who is actually in control of the situation.

The acting is top notch, and the way the tension builds up slowly makes the shocks hit harder. Some might find the middle part a bit slow, but the payoff is totally worth it. If you love stories where a polite conversation turns into a nightmare, you need to see this.
endingExplained: The young man finally reveals that he is not just a fan, but a sociopath who wants to live out a Ripley story in real life. He tries to kill Highsmith to prove he is a better criminal than her characters. However, Highsmith reveals she saw through him the whole time. She outsmarts him using her own plotting skills, leading to his capture. She wins the game, proving the author is always the boss.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves psychological games and crime stories.
